newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Expert says lowers Metway value.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Expert says lowers Metway value.

text.p: The independent expert valuing the proposed merger between Metway Bank Ltd and the Queensland government's Suncorp Finance and the Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) said it has lowered its valuation for Metway from the bank's valuation made in April.

Grant Samuel and Associates said it valued Metway between A$685 million and A$760 million, compared with the valuation of between A$710 million and A$810 million it estimated in April when Metway was under a bid from St George Bank Ltd.
It said the lower valuation was due to the deteriorating outlook for Australian regional banks.

"The outlook for regional bank profits has deteriorated slightly since that time, principally due to a decline in net interest margins caused by continuing competition from the major banks and specialist home loan originators," Grant Samuel said.
"This has been reflected in a slight downturn in the market ratings of regional banks and a reduction in Grant Samuel's valuation of Metway Bak to the range A$685-A$760 million."

It said this valuation reflects the full underlying value of Metway. The valuation incorporates a premium for control and is in excess of the level at which shares in Metway Bank would be expected to trade under current market conditions.
The enlarged group from Metway's proposed complex merger with Suncorp and QIDC would have a market capitalisation of A$2.2 billion, Grant Samuel said.
This valuation is based on the share price equivalent to the cash payment of A$4.80 per Metway share from the Queensland government, it said.

It said its valuation of Metway's banking operations represent multiples of 12.5-13.9 times forecast 1996/97 after tax earnings and multiples of 1.6-1.8 times the net tangible assets of Metway as at June 30, 1996.
It said the combined value of Suncorp and QIDC has been estimated in the range of A$1.53-A$1.69 billion.
